title: Delta Steering: Latency-first Geo Pinning with Capacity-aware Fallthrough
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We currently have coarse geo-routing and several ad-hoc capacity fallbacks that cause spike-induced latency regressions and cross-region cost blowouts. This ticket proposes a new routing policy (Delta Steering) that prefers the nearest region by latency but enforces capacity-aware fallthroughs and token-level circuit breaking to avoid cascading overloads and protect SLOs.

Goals:
- Meet p95 latency SLOs (region-local) for latency-sensitive routes while keeping global cost within budget.
- Provide deterministic, debuggable failover behavior when local capacity is constrained.
- Integrate with existing circuit-breaker signals and autoscaling hints so routing decisions respond to real capacity telemetry.
- Enable safe canaries and incremental rollout with telemetry-backed guardrails.

Scope:
- New steering policy implementation in request director service.
- New routing config schema exposed via control plane and Console.
- Telemetry/metrics + dashboards for policy evaluation and regression alerts.
- Controlled rollout to latency-sensitive customer routes, starting with internal staging and select customers.

Out of scope:
- New autoscaler algorithms (we will consume existing autoscaler hints).
- Major data-plane runtime changes beyond metadata in routing layer.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Director applies Delta Steering config and routes >95% of eligible requests to latency-preferred region under normal capacity.
2) When preferred region reports >85% GPU-util or token-queue-length exceeds threshold, requests fallthrough to next-best region(s) following capacity-aware score rather than purely latency.
3) Circuit breakers trip at token-level degradation (latency moving percentile > configured window) and immediately divert traffic to fallback path without global fail-open.
4) No observable p95 regression for unaffected regions during rollout.
5) Console shows per-route policy decisions + per-region capacity hints and a timeline for fallthrough decisions.
6) Automated regression alert fires if policy causes >5% error-rate increase or p95 latency regression across affected routes.
tasks: Design routing score: score = latency_penalty + capacity_penalty + affinity_bonus (documented in RFC)
Implement control-plane schema changes to store Delta Steering policies (support weights, thresholds, fallthrough order)
Add capacity hint consumer in Director: GPU util, token-queue length, pending-batch-count
Implement token-level circuit breaker hook and soft-shed signal in Director
Integrate tracing: emit route.reason and route.score components per request
Create Console dashboard: per-route decision distribution, capacity hint heatmap, canary health view
Run staged canary: internal -> 5% customer subset -> gradually 25% -> 100% if metrics pass
Write e2e tests and chaos scenarios (region isolates, capacity spike)
notes:
Design trade-offs:
- We choose a latency-first objective because many product flows are latency-sensitive; capacity penalty is additive but tuned to avoid cross-region cost runaway.
- Conservative thresholds: initial capacity threshold = 85% util and token-backlog multiplier = 3x baseline. These will be exposed as policy knobs.
- Soft-shedding is preferred over hard-rejects: a low-priority request may be downgraded to cached response or queued with a client-visible Retry-After header.

Config example (conceptual):
policy: delta-steering
preferred_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
latency_weight: 0.7
capacity_weight: 0.25
affinity_bonus: 0.05
capacity_thresholds: {util: 0.85, backlog_mult: 3}
cb_window_ms: 30000
cb_latency_p95_delta_ms: 120
risks_mitigation:
Risks:
- Incorrect thresholds could cause oscillation across regions -> mitigation: add hysteresis window (cooldown per-route) and sticky grace period after failover.
- Cross-region cost increase -> mitigation: set global budget safety cap, per-tenant cost alarms and fallback to cheaper-compatible model variants.
- Observability gaps -> mitigation: mandatory tracing fields + synthetic traffic test harness for each canary phase.

Fallback plan: rollback policy config and re-enable last-known-good routing matrix; if Director code causes instability, rollback codepath on control plane and divert to simple geo-pin policy.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch + RFC + design doc in Confluence (link included in comments).
2) Unit + integration tests; internal staging deployment with synthetic load tests.
3) Canary to internal traffic (2 days), then to 5% external customer traffic (3 days), monitor metrics.
4) Expand to 25% then 100% if no regressions; each step gated by automated smoke checks.
5) Post-rollout: 72-hour monitoring window and PR with lessons learned.
metrics_and_telemetry:
Emit the following metrics (per-route, per-region):
- route.decision.count (preferred|fallthrough|circuit_tripped)
- route.score.components (latency, capacity, affinity) histogram
- region.capacity.utilization (GPU-util)
- region.token_queue_length
- route.latency.p50/p95/p99
- route.error_rate
- policy.fallback_rate
Create Dashboard panels: policy decision distribution, capacity trend lines, canary smoke results. Create alerts: p95 increase >10% or error_rate increase >5% within 15m.
